messages:
alex: Quick sync — Datadog SI asked for a drop-in OpenTelemetry pipeline pattern for our private HW appliance marketplace bundle. They want a minimal collector + exporters example and guidance on sampling and span naming. Can we draft something that’s safe for air-gapped installs?

maria: Yes. Key constraints: must not ship secrets, should support local file fallback for exporters, and include hw resource attributes (hw.vendor, hw.model, hw.gpu_count). Sampling: recommend 100% for errors, 1% for successful inference traces, and 10% for long-tail slow requests.

sam: I can assemble a minimal collector config. Will include a file exporter and a datadog exporter block that we comment out for air-gapped customers. Pushing a draft to GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-templates/pull/82 (WIP)

jordan: For dashboarding we need clear span names and metric labels. Suggest span names: inference.request, model.kv_cache.lookup, model.tokenize, model.generate. Metric labels: model_name, quantization, hw_pool. Also add token_rate and kv_hit_ratio gauges.

dd-integ-bot: Datadog integration checklist updated: https://internal.datadog/checks/ri-otel. Items added: export schema versioning, sample rate guidance, tag mapping.

alex: Marketplace listing requires we state which telemetry is available out of the box vs opt-in. Keep APM (traces) opt-in for private bundles; metrics can be vendored as local exporters. Also legal wants a short blurb about PII redaction — ensure we include a note in the sample config.

maria: Draft OTEL snippet (shortened):
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols: { grpc: {}, http: {} }
processors:
  batch: {}
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: http.request.header.authorization
        action: delete
exporters:
  file:
    path: /var/log/telemetry/otlp-out.json
  datadog:
    api:
      key: "<REDACTED>" # comment out for air-gap
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [file, datadog]
```
Add comment: enable datadog exporter only when customer provides credentials; otherwise rely on file exporter + partner ingestion job.

sam: Smokes scheduled: I'll run the collector on sim-hw nodes Friday 11:00 PDT and post logs. Test plan: 1) ensure file exporter writes spans; 2) ensure attributes include hw.* tags; 3) validate sampling config toggles.

jordan: I'll create a dashboard tile JSON and a lightweight readme for marketplace docs: include example queries for token_rate and kv_hit_ratio, and a trace view focused on inference.request waterfall. Will tag dashboard with metadata: partner:datadog, market:hardware, privacy:airgap-friendly.

alex: Assignment recap: @maria sample config + redaction guidance (PR today), @sam smoke test + logs (Fri 11am), @jordan dashboard tile + marketplace docs (ETA EOW). @legal to provide final wording for listing. Everyone OK with that timeline?

maria: OK, PR opened and linked above. I added a note about removing Authorization headers and hashing user identifiers.

sam: On it. Will post run artifacts here after the test. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment staging/collector-sim-hw succeeded (run-873). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/run/873/artifacts

alex: Excellent. After the smoke pass we'll draft a short partner-runbook and a joint announcement blurb that focuses on "observability-ready hardware bundles". Thanks all — keep updates in this thread.
